VM: LAB_READY was present. Two boots ran on Win10 22H2 10.0.19045.2965 with wininet 11.0.19041.2193. The first COM1 byte arrives at about 34 s. Whole boots took 50 s and 63 s on the host.

Loopback over IPv4 and IPv6 works. Windows Firewall is ON for all profiles and Defender is running, but neither interfered with 127.0.0.1/::1 servers. Recommendation: bind loopback only, never 0.0.0.0.

'localhost' resolves to ::1 first, and a refused loopback connect on Windows takes about 2 s. So wininet to localhost against a v4-only server took 2031-2044 ms, and against a server on both ::1 and 127.0.0.1 with the same port it took 0.7 ms. The server library must listen dual-stack, and URLs should default to 127.0.0.1. A refused-connect test costs 2010 ms (12029), or 4093 ms via localhost.

No WPAD delay: proxy flags are 0x9 (auto-detect on), but PRECONFIG costs the same as DIRECT. WinHttpDetectAutoProxyConfigUrl fails with 12180 in 0.4 ms, and NXDOMAIN gives 12007 in under 3 ms. Loopback bypasses the proxy implicitly (decomp: IsLoopbackMacro '<-loopback>'). Still use INTERNET_OPEN_TYPE_DIRECT outside proxy areas.
Image settings in HKCU Internet Settings: SecureProtocols=0x800 (wininet uses TLS 1.2 only) and CertificateRevocation=1. Tests that need TLS 1.0/1.1 must set the protocols explicitly.

Schannel server works headless as Administrator. CertCreateSelfSignCertificate (sha256RSA) worked with a CAPI key (AT_KEYEXCHANGE) and with a CNG key. AcquireCredentialsHandle(SECPKG_CRED_INBOUND) succeeded with SCHANNEL_CRED v4 and with SCH_CREDENTIALS v5. The session negotiated TLS 1.2 with suite 0xC030. Key containers were deleted afterwards.

HTTPS errors with a CN=localhost cert and no SAN, against 127.0.0.1: 12045 (INVALID_CA), then 12038 (CN_INVALID) after adding 0x100 (IGNORE_UNKNOWN_CA), then 200 after adding 0x1000. localhost needs only 0x100. With a SAN of DNS:localhost + IP:127.0.0.1, both names need only 0x100. After success the security flags read 0x20000101 (or 0x20001101 when CN was also ignored).

Ignore flags are not remembered across requests or sessions on the same host:port (12045 comes back). Setting INTERNET_OPTION_SECURITY_FLAGS on the session handle fails with 12018. INTERNET_OPTION_SECURITY_CONNECTION_INFO needs the full 716-byte struct (with SecPkgContext_CipherInfo); the short layout gets error 122.

wininet aborts mid-handshake when cert verification fails, so the TLS server must treat EOF as normal. Wire capture: InternetOpenUrl sends only the request line, User-Agent, Host:port and Cache-Control: no-cache. Connection: Keep-Alive appeared only on a re-sent request handle (observation only, not explained).
FTP over loopback with PASV works. The client sends USER, PASS, PWD, TYPE A, PASV, LIST (no SYST or FEAT).
The guest clock is about 1 h behind the host. Use only guest time (GetSystemTime) for expiry, cookie and cert tests.
Serial throughput: unbuffered printf > COM1 is 38 KB/s. Buffered output or a direct COM1 write is about 245 KB/s. Through the vmrun pipe, 2 MB took 8.9 s.
COM1 is exclusive: a second writer gets 'Access is denied', the output is lost, and errorlevel is still 0.

Results-protocol decision: a guest runner, vmrun.exe. It owns COM1 and frames each exe as @@I7 BEGIN/END with exit, ms and timeout. The child runs in a kill-on-close job and is killed at its deadline. Verified: a hang was killed at 5 s (0xDEAD0001); a crash reported 0xC0000005 with no WER stall. tools/vm_run.sh then splits the frames into results/<area>.txt.

The doc specifies the server library: common/srv.h, resolved at runtime rather than import-linked, with scripted per-connection steps, a wire recorder with parsed header order and casing, cert profiles, FTP, and stop that returns within 3 s plus a lifetime cap. It also covers port selection and a risk table. wininet.h and winhttp.h cannot be included in the same translation unit.

result.name: 02_win10_semantics
keyFindings: I wrote /home/iceisfun/industrial7_test_wininet/docs/research/02_win10_semantics.md (about 600 lines) and committed it on master as 240ee37. It is not pushed and touches only that file. I did not run the Win10 VM in this role.

Every statement carries a tag. [D fn@rva] means read from the docker1 decomp. [W10] means a genuine-Win10 row from lane G, copied in 03_prior_data_and_i7.md. [K] means general WinINet knowledge that still needs a VM run. [VM?] means an open question or a disagreement.

Correction to an earlier lane: InternetCrackUrlW on Win10 is the normal 4-argument SDK form (D @0x2d690). The '14-argument form' in industrial7 WININET-W10-LINK.md and in doc 03 is a misreading of the internal CrackUrl helper. The A version requires dwStructSize==0x68. The W version does not check it and writes 0x68 back.

Handles and errors: HINTERNET values are small integers counted from 0x00CC0004 in steps of 4 (D MapHandleToAddress), not pointers. A bad or closed handle gives 6, and the wrong handle type gives 12018. Each handle type has a 4-char tag (Inet, HCon, FCon, HReq, HRlf, FFil, ...), which maps to the INTERNET_OPTION_HANDLE_TYPE values 1/4/2/13/14/7. InternetOpen success sets last error to 0.

W functions mostly convert their strings and call the A function, so length units are where A and W differ. HttpQueryInfoW reports bytes: on success without the NUL, on 122 with the NUL. InternetQueryOptionW and InternetCreateUrlW report characters on success but bytes on 122. On success InternetGetCookieExW appears to return characters including the NUL; this is flagged [VM?].

HttpOpenRequest rules, all offline-testable: a NULL or empty verb becomes GET and a NULL object becomes '/'. A verb with bytes after the token gives 87, and TRACE or TRACK gives 12016. Verb matching is case-sensitive, so 'get' counts as an unknown method. Methods other than GET/POST get RELOAD|NO_CACHE_WRITE added. If the connect port is one of 19,21,25,110,119,143,220,465,990,993,995, HttpOpenRequest fails with 12005. Accept types are joined with commas, and the referrer becomes a Referer header.

Headers added at send time (D InitBeginSendRequest): User-Agent is the trimmed agent string, added only if the caller did not supply one, and omitted when the agent is NULL. Host is 'host', or 'host:port' when the port is not 80/443. Content-Length is set from the body or dwBufferTotal, and is 0 for methods other than GET/HEAD with no body. DNT is added only under policy. Accept-Encoding is added only when HTTP_DECODING is on. The exact wire order still needs recording on the VM.

Redirects: 301/302 turn POST into GET. 303 always uses GET. 307/308 keep the method. Following a redirect with any method other than GET, HEAD or POST, or 307/308 with POST, gives 12168. When the redirect budget runs out the error is 12156. NO_COOKIES skips storing Set-Cookie headers, and NO_AUTH skips the 401/407 handling.

HttpQueryInfo validation table: a level above 0x5F (other than CUSTOM) gives 87. Seven invalid modifier combinations give 87. A modifier not allowed for that level gives 12154. STATUS_CODE or STATUS_TEXT with FLAG_REQUEST_HEADERS gives 12154. A non-zero index with COALESCE_WITH_COMMA gives 12150. A CUSTOM header name with a control character or space gives 87. A missing header gives 12150. A string reply too small gives 122 with the length including the NUL; on success the length excludes it. W with FLAG_NUMBER64 returns garbled data and must never be CHECKed.

The option table lists, per option: valid handle types, size, and errors. Read-only options give 12011. Options outside 1..0xC0 give 12009. A NULL handle on a non-process-wide option gives 12018. A wrong DWORD length gives 12010. Options 15/16/26/30/78 give 120, and 54-57/70 give 50. Setting USER_AGENT to an empty string gives 12010. MAX_CONNS set to 0 gives 160 and other values are clamped to 2..128. CONNECT_TIMEOUT 0 on the global setting is silently ignored. SECURITY_FLAGS can only add the ignore bits 0x13380. For W string options the set length is in characters.

Dates: InternetTimeFromSystemTime checks the buffer size first (A <30, W <60 gives 122), then the 87 checks. It takes the weekday from the caller's wDayOfWeek unless wDay > 6. InternetTimeToSystemTime fills fields from the clock only when the string has fewer than 4 fields (fewer than 2 means the whole value). Two-digit years below 80 become 20xx. The weekday comes from the name, not recomputed. Out-of-range fields give 87. This matches the W10 task 65 rows.

Crack, canonicalize and cookies: unless the caller asks for ExtraInfo, the CrackUrl path keeps the ?query and #fragment. Ports above 65535 or with non-digits give 12005, and a missing ':' gives 12006. A file: URL path is converted with PathCreateFromUrlW (C:\...). Canonicalize/Combine escape by default (ICU_NO_ENCODE turns escaping off). Canonicalize has no size-query mode (*len==0 gives 87). E_POINTER maps to 122 and other failures to 87. Setting an HttpOnly cookie without INTERNET_COOKIE_HTTPONLY returns state 5 with error 4317. GetCookieEx with no match gives 259; a non-NULL reserved argument or NULL size gives 87.

Section 16 lists 12 disagreements and open items for the VM pass. The main one: the decomp says HttpQueryInfo before send gives 12019, but W10 task 64 saw success. Others: A InternetConnect with an empty server gives 87 but W gives 123; EXPIRES with the SYSTEMTIME flag always failed with 12154; the CrackUrlW dwStructSize behaviour; cookie W length units; 307 POST; the exact default-header order.

keyFindings: Enumeration filter rule from the CCacheEntryEnum::Next decomp: an entry is returned only if (dwFilter & type) == type. FindFirstUrlCacheEntryA/W always pass the filter 0x300035, so EDITED and SPARSE entries never appear through them.

Enumeration handles are odd table indices, (idx<<1)|1. A bogus, closed or wrong-type handle fails with ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE (6). FindNextUrlCacheEntry with a NULL handle fails with 87. FindCloseUrlCache(NULL) fails with 6. The container APIs report an invalid handle as 87.

When a conversion fails with 122, the enumeration cursor does not advance, so the same entry comes back on retry. A FindFirst size query also closes its handle. On success *size is set to the exact required size, and the A form follows 0x70 + al4(url+1) + al4(file+1) + al4(ext+1) + al4(hdr).

FIND_FLAGS 0x2 (struct only) needs at least 0x70 bytes. It zeroes the caller's whole buffer, leaves the string pointers NULL and does not rewrite *size. FIND_FLAGS 0x4 (fixed part plus file name) needs at least 0x174 bytes and is checked first when both bits are set.

Groups: CreateUrlCacheGroup rejects any flag outside 0x7 and a non-NULL reserved pointer with 87. GIDONLY returns the next id without creating a group or advancing the counter. NONPURGEABLE sets bit 0x1000000000000000 in the id, and adding an entry to such a group sets STICKY_CACHE_ENTRY on it. Ids that are invalid or missing fail with 2.

GetUrlCacheGroupAttribute always sets *cb to 0x9c (A) or 0x114 (W) and fails with 122 if the buffer is smaller. It never writes dwGroupSize. Each attribute bit writes its own set of fields (table in groups.c).

Possible quirk: SetUrlCacheGroupAttribute copies the group name into its request only when the QUOTA bit (8) is set, but the server stores the name when GROUPNAME (0x10) is set. Not yet checked on the VM.

Other decomp findings: GetUrlCacheEntryBinaryBlob returns a Win32 error code rather than a BOOL and clears all outputs first. FreeUrlCacheSpace with a percentage above 100 fails with 87. FindFirstUrlCacheContainer with the NOCHANGE option and an unchanged counter fails with 12051.

WinINet has no redirect-policy or max-redirects option. Option 89 (the WinHTTP number for max redirects) is accepted on a session handle but does not change the limit. Option 88 can be set only on a request handle. Neither can be queried (error 87).

301, 302, 303 and 307 without a Location header: the body is drained, then HttpSendRequest fails with 12150 ERROR_HTTP_HEADER_NOT_FOUND. The decomp checks for a Location header before redirecting 300 and 308, so a 308 without Location comes back as ordinary data with its body.

A RetrieveUrlCacheEntryFile or Stream call that fails with 122 still adds a hit but leaves no lock. GetUrlCacheEntryInfo and GetUrlCacheEntryInfoEx never lock and never add a hit.

keyFindings: Issued certificate chains are partial on the client: the schannel server sends only the leaf, even with the untrusted issuer in its credential store. With 0x100 every issued leaf then fails with 12057 (SEC_CERT_REV_FAILED); 0x180 (IGNORE_UNKNOWN_CA|IGNORE_REVOCATION) succeeds. Chain status is 0x1010040 after the 12057 failure and 0x10000 after a 0x180 success.

No CRL is ever fetched under an untrusted root, whether the chain is partial or completed via AIA. A 404, a closed port, a valid CRL and a CRL revoking the leaf all give 12057, and 0x80 clears it. 12170 (REVOKED) cannot be reached without trusting the root, so it needs a dx_ area.

An AIA caIssuers URL makes CryptoAPI fetch the issuer (GET /issuer.crt, User-Agent Microsoft-CryptoAPI/10.0, Accept */*, Connection Keep-Alive). The chain then has 2 elements with error 0x20 and info 0x100. An expired issuer gives 12037 until 0x2000 is set.

Errors surface one at a time in a fixed order: wrong usage 12169, then date 12037, then CN 12038, then revocation 12057. Retry on one handle goes 12045 -> 12037 -> 12038 -> 12057 -> 200, with one TCP connection per attempt.

Name matching: a SAN with only DNS entries does not match an IP host. A SAN with only an IP entry still lets the host name match the CN. CN-only certificates match by CN, including the IP literal. The wildcards *, *host, local* and *.localhost do not match localhost. 'localhost.' matches, consistent with the decomp's trailing-dot strip in VerifyTrust.

An MD5-signed leaf fails the handshake with 12157 whatever the flags. SHA-1, SHA-384 and RSA-1024 leaves behave like SHA-256. anyExtendedKeyUsage is accepted; clientAuth-only and codeSigning-only leaves give 12169.

Decomp: InternetQueryOptionW forwards option 32 to the A function, so the W struct holds ANSI strings (also confirmed on the VM). MapInternetError maps CRYPT_E_REVOCATION_OFFLINE to 12057 and TRUST_E_CERT_SIGNATURE to 12169 (12062 for a weak-signature chain). 12055 and 12062 come only from VerifyTrust's multi-error loop, which needs an internal socket flag no public option was found to set, so they are decomp-only.
Async HTTPS: certificate and TLS errors arrive as REQUEST_COMPLETE with dwResult 0. Status sequence for 12045 is 80 20 21 50 51 100; for a success it is 80 20 21 30 31 40 41 100.

INTERNET_FLAG_SECURE on InternetConnect is ignored (plain HTTP is sent, giving 12152). INTERNET_FLAG_IGNORE_REDIRECT_TO_HTTP/HTTPS do not change cross-scheme redirects. A chunked HttpSendRequestEx upload still sends Content-Length: 0.
